suggestions.rationale: Cross-sectional population research has reported a significant association between migraine and obsessive-compulsive disorder, but it does not establish directionality and does not show that OCD caused or aggravated an individual veteran's migraine disorder. The application should therefore keep this draft mapping association-focused and require case-specific diagnosis, chronology, competing-cause assessment, and medical opinion before any individual secondary theory is advanced.
evidenceGaps: Clinician-documented migraine diagnosis and headache history
Documentation establishing the OCD diagnosis, severity and timing relative to migraine onset
Neurology or other qualified medical opinion addressing causation or aggravation in the individual case

sourceReferences.citation: Goulart AC, Santos IS, Brunoni AR, et al. Migraine headaches and mood/anxiety disorders in the ELSA Brazil. Headache. 2014;54(8):1310-1319. PMID 24898830
sourceReferences.note: Cross-sectional ELSA-Brasil analysis compared 1,261 participants with definite migraine with 10,531 controls and found significant associations between migraine and several psychiatric disorders including OCD. Supports association only, not OCD-to-migraine directionality or individual causation/aggravation.

sourceReferences.note: Official legal framework for secondary service connection and aggravation; it does not establish the underlying medical OCD-to-migraine relationship.

suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-15 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. A nationally representative survey found obsessive-compulsive disorder associated with substantial comorbidity with mood disorders; the approved relationship is limited to population-level comorbidity association and does not establish onset order, direction, or individual causation. Require independently established obsessive-compulsive disorder and separately established depressive disorder; the cited nationally representative survey reported substantial comorbidity of OCD with mood disorders as a class and does not establish onset order or direction. Preserve other anxiety disorders, substance use, medical illness, medications, and shared vulnerability as competing explanations. Do not infer a depressive disorder from OCD symptoms or distress alone, and do not treat this population-level association as proof that OCD caused an individual's depressive disorder. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of ocd and depressive-disorder
Chronology compatible with the approved bounded proposition
Assessment of shared risk factors, reverse direction, treatment effects, and other competing causes
